summary.short: Executive Order 14117 directs the Attorney General to issue regulations restricting U.S. persons' transactions that give countries of concern or covered persons access to Americans' bulk sensitive personal data or US Government-related data. DHS/CISA must publish security requirements for restricted transactions. Signed 28 February 2024.
summary.long: Sets national-security restrictions on access by countries of concern to Americans' bulk sensitive personal data and US Government-related data, under IEEPA and the national emergency in EO 13873. Section 2 directs the Attorney General, with DHS, to issue regulations that prohibit or restrict U.S. persons' transactions involving such data or classes of transactions posing unacceptable risk. Regulations must define terms, identify countries of concern and covered persons, create licensing, and address recordkeeping; they may not impose generalized data localization. A proposed rule is due within 180 days. DHS/CISA must publish security requirements for restricted transactions based on NIST frameworks. Evasion, conspiracy and knowingly directing prohibited transactions are also prohibited. Section 3 directs the Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation in the US Telecommunications Services Sector to prioritise reviews of submarine cable licences linked to countries of concern; agencies are to consider limiting federal healthcare and research assistance that enables such access; the CFPB is encouraged to address data brokers. Sections 4 to 6 require recommendations on prior transfers, reports to the President, and an assessment of other human 'omic data. Section 8 creates no enforceable rights. The order states no penalty amounts; enforcement terms are left to implementing regulations.

notes: Operative provisions largely delegate key terms to later Attorney General regulations: the bulk threshold (Sec. 7(b)), countries of concern (Sec. 7(c)), covered personal identifiers (Sec. 7(e)), human ’omic data (Sec. 7(i)) and the prohibited and restricted transaction classes (Sec. 2(a)-(c)). No numeric threshold, penalty amount or effective date is stated in this text. Sec. 2(g)(v) excludes non-genomic ’omic data pending the Sec. 6 report. Timing in Secs. 4 and 5 runs from the effective date of regulations under Sec. 2(c), which the text does not date. Sec. 8(e) states the order creates no enforceable right. Entities listed are those with operative duties; consultation-only bodies (e.g., Treasury, Commerce, FBI) are omitted. Sec. 1 and Sec. 2(g)(iii) disclaim generalized data localization. Federal Register print artifacts (header lines, 'ddrumheller' tags, 'BIDEN.EPS' graphic tag) are not coded.

enforcement.note: The order states no fine, criminal penalty, licence revocation, clawback, suspension or blocking sanction. Sec. 2(i) and 2(j) declare evasion and conspiracy prohibited, and Sec. 2(b) authorizes the Attorney General to use IEEPA powers, but no penalty amount or sanction regime is specified; enforcement is left to implementing regulations not contained in this text.
